title: Services to a public company — Summit Industries
instructions: Dale & Frost LLP audits **Summit Industries**, an SEC registrant. Summit's audit committee has asked about additional services and staffing changes. Evaluate each item under SEC and PCAOB rules, then review the draft memo to the audit committee.

exhibits.title: Requests from Summit
exhibits.content:
1. Prepare Summit's federal and state income tax returns.
2. Perform a valuation of intangible assets acquired in a business combination.
3. Perform Summit's internal audit function for one year.
4. Issue a comfort letter for a planned bond offering.
5. Prepare the personal tax return of Summit's CFO.
6. Provide expert testimony in Summit's patent litigation.
7. Design and implement Summit's new financial reporting system.

exhibits.title: Staffing facts
exhibits.content:
- Partner Ames has led the audit for 5 consecutive years.
- Partner Brooks, the engagement quality reviewer, has served 3 years.
- Partner Cho (another audit partner) has served 7 consecutive years.

rows.label: 1. Corporate income tax returns
rows.explanation: Tax compliance is permitted, subject to pre-approval and the PCAOB tax rules.

rows.label: 2. Valuation of intangibles
rows.explanation: Valuation services would have the auditor audit its own work.

rows.label: 3. Internal audit outsourcing
rows.explanation: Internal audit outsourcing is a prohibited service.

rows.label: 4. Comfort letter
rows.explanation: An audit-related service that is permitted.

rows.label: 5. CFO's personal return
rows.explanation: PCAOB Rule 3523: no tax services to a person in a financial reporting oversight role.

rows.label: 6. Expert testimony in patent litigation
rows.explanation: Expert services unrelated to the audit are prohibited (advocacy).

rows.label: 7. Financial reporting system design
rows.explanation: Financial information systems design and implementation is prohibited.

parts.prompt: Review the draft memo to Summit's audit committee. Correct any errors.

segments.text: **To the Audit Committee — Partner rotation.** Partner Ames has served as lead engagement partner for five years and

segments.original: may continue for two more years
options: may continue for two more years
must rotate off the engagement for five years
must rotate off the engagement for two years
segments.answer: must rotate off the engagement for five years
segments.explanation: Lead partners serve a maximum of 5 consecutive years, followed by a 5-year time-out.

segments.text: . Partner Brooks, the engagement quality reviewer,

options: may continue for two more years
segments.answer: may continue for two more years
segments.explanation: The EQR partner has served only 3 of the 5 permitted years.

segments.text: . Partner Cho has served seven years and

segments.original: must rotate off for two years
options: must rotate off for two years
must rotate off for five years
segments.answer: must rotate off for two years
segments.explanation: Other audit partners: 7 years on, 2 years off.

segments.text: . All audit and permitted nonaudit services

segments.original: may be approved by the CFO
options: may be approved by the CFO
must be pre-approved by the audit committee
need approval only if fees exceed audit fees
segments.answer: must be pre-approved by the audit committee
segments.explanation: SOX Section 202 requires audit committee pre-approval; it cannot be delegated to management.
